title: Particle Detection - Stacking Faults Detection on ICOS T3/T7
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 22nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the ICOS T3/T7 system to detect and classify Stacking Faults defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 22nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Stacking Faults defects that are critical to yield at the 22nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the ICOS T3/T7 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: ICOS T3/T7
- Inspection Type: Particle Detection
- Target Defect: Stacking Faults
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 22nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all ICOS T3/T7 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-oxidation monitoring in the 22nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: ICOS T3/T7
Software Version: v9.7.257
Recipe: PARTICLE_DETECTION_22nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (122 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the ICOS T3/T7 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Particle Detection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Stacking Faults defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 22nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 63 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.8% for Particle Detection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-08-16
Wafers Tested: 22
Total Defects Found: 3063
Defect Density: 433.33 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.2%
Capture Rate: 90.3%
Test Duration: 213 minutes
System Uptime: 99.9%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The ICOS T3/T7 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Stacking Faults at the 22nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
